learning_objective: 🎯 Witness a powerful revolt against caste oppression and spiritual blindness as a marginalized woman discovers her inherent human dignity through a Buddhist monk's simple request!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Prakriti is an 'untouchable' Chandal girl who has internalized society's scorn. Her life transforms when Ananda, a disciple of Gautama Buddha, asks her for water, reminding her that all human beings share the same pure water and equal birthright.
Tagore uses Prakriti's anger to critique rigid Hindu orthodox caste rules. Once awakened to her self-worth, she refuses to accept her marginalization as karma or divine punishment.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🔮 The Conflict of Desire and Magic
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Overwhelmed by her new feelings, Prakriti mistakes her gratitude for romantic obsession. She forces her mother, Maya, to use dark primordial magic to drag Ananda back to her home against his will.

When Ananda arrives, his face is distorted by agony from the dark spell. Seeing the moral destruction of the man who gave her light, Prakriti feels deep remorse, breaks the spell, and asks for forgiveness, realizing true love means freedom, not possession.

fun_activity.title: 💧 The Water Test
fun_activity.instructions: Ananda asks for water saying it is the same for every human. Think about modern barriers—social, economic, or cultural. Write down one way we can break a 'barrier' of inequality in our daily school or work life!

exam_tips: 📌 Explain Ananda's famous teaching to Prakriti: 'Do not humiliate yourself; self-humiliation is a sin worse than self-murder.'
📌 Contrast Prakriti's initial rebellion (seeking human dignity) with her later flaw (possessive desire that harms another's spiritual freedom).
📌 Note the role of Prakriti's mother, Maya, who warns her daughter against using dark sorcery against a pure spiritual monk, eventually sacrificing her own life in the process.
quick_recap: ⭐ The play is based on an ancient Buddhist legend from the Divyavadana.
⭐ Tagore weaves together themes of social equality, psychological obsession, and spiritual liberation.
⭐ The ending shows Prakriti achieving true spiritual maturity by letting go of her selfish attachment.
